questions.text: What is an exception in Python?
options: An error that happens while the program runs and stops it, unless we handle it
A line that Python skips on purpose
A warning that Python shows but then ignores
A special kind of variable for errors

questions.text: Python runs a `try` block and one of its lines fails. What does it do next?
options: It runs the rest of the try block, then the except block
It runs the failing line again
It jumps to the except block and runs that code instead

questions.text: In a `try` block, what happens to the lines after the one that fails?
options: They run after the except block
They run before the except block
They never run: Python leaves the try block at the failing line
They run only when the try block is inside a loop

questions.text: Why is `except ValueError:` often better than a bare `except:`?
options: It runs faster than a bare except
A bare except catches only ValueError
Only except ValueError can be used inside a loop
We know exactly what went wrong, and each error can get its own message

questions.text: When does the code under `else:` run, after `try` and `except`?

questions.text: When does the code under `finally:` run?
options: No matter what: with an error or without one
Only at the very end of the program
